sources.entry: The Copenhagen Book provides a general guideline on implementing auth in web applications

summary.title: The Copenhagen Book
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source, community-maintained guideline on implementing authentication for web applications, meant to be read alongside the OWASP Cheat Sheet Series.
keywords: how to implement login for websites
takeaways: It is a general guideline for implementing auth in web applications.
The content is free, open-source, and community-maintained.
It may be opinionated or incomplete in places, according to the site.
The authors recommend using it together with the OWASP Cheat Sheet Series.
Suggestions or concerns can be raised by opening an issue.
summary.summary: The Copenhagen Book is a free, open-source guideline on implementing authentication in web applications, created by Pilcrow and maintained by the community. The page states that it may be opinionated or incomplete at times, and that it aims to fill a gap in online resources. The site recommends using it alongside the OWASP Cheat Sheet Series. The landing text does not list specific topics or code examples, so the detailed contents could not be confirmed from this page alone.
